questions.stem: The following organisms do practice basking except
questions.explanation: Bats are endothermic mammals; lizards, snakes and crocodiles are ectotherms that bask in the sun to warm up.

questions.stem: Kangaroo is an example of
questions.explanation: Kangaroos are marsupials (pouched mammals), classified under Metatheria.

questions.stem: The following are characteristics of chordates except
questions.explanation: Chordate characteristics are the postanal tail, notochord, dorsal nerve cord and pharyngeal slits; 'pinochord' is not a structure.

questions.stem: Wuchereria bancrofti is an example of phylum
questions.explanation: Wuchereria bancrofti, the filarial worm causing elephantiasis, belongs to the phylum Nematoda.

questions.stem: The following are flagellates except
questions.explanation: Euglena, Trypanosoma and Leishmania are flagellates (class Mastigophora); Plasmodium is an apicomplexan (Sporozoa) and moves by gliding, not flagella.

questions.stem: Hydra belongs to the class
questions.explanation: Hydra is a freshwater cnidarian of the class Hydrozoa.

questions.stem: Cephalization is first observed in the Phylum
questions.explanation: Cephalization (concentration of sense organs at the head end) first appears in the Platyhelminthes, the flatworms.

questions.stem: The fusion of head and thorax is called
questions.explanation: The fusion of head and thorax is the cephalothorax, seen in crustaceans and spiders.

questions.stem: Taenia solium infects
questions.explanation: Taenia solium, the pork tapeworm, infects humans through undercooked pork.

questions.stem: Radula is found in the Phylum
questions.explanation: The radula, a rasping tongue-like feeding structure, is characteristic of the phylum Mollusca.

questions.stem: Platypus is an example of
questions.explanation: The platypus is an egg-laying mammal, a monotreme.

questions.stem: Reptiles possess dry skin and scales to prevent
questions.explanation: Dry scaly skin in reptiles reduces cutaneous water loss (evaporation) - an adaptation to terrestrial life.

questions.stem: Ecdysis is found in
questions.explanation: Ecdysis (moulting of the exoskeleton) occurs in arthropods.

questions.stem: The exoskeleton found in Arthropods is called
questions.explanation: The arthropod exoskeleton is the cuticle, made of chitin.

questions.stem: Open circulatory system is found in the following organisms except
questions.explanation: Reptiles have a closed circulatory system; snails, crustaceans and insects have open systems.

questions.stem: Earthworm is an example of
questions.explanation: The earthworm is an oligochaete annelid (few bristles per segment).

questions.stem: The repetition of cells and organs in various segments of an organism is called
questions.explanation: Metamerism is the repetition of body segments (serial homology).

questions.stem: Scientists decide whether an organism is a plant or animal based on

options.A: whether it is multicellular or unicellular
options.B: whether it is mobile or not
options.D: how it obtains its food or energy

questions.explanation: Modern biology separates plants from animals mainly by mode of nutrition: plants are autotrophic, animals heterotrophic.

questions.stem: You are given an unstained slide of an unknown plant cell. Even with careful focus adjustments, you are able to make out only one large round structure within the cell. This is most likely to be the
questions.explanation: In an unstained preparation, the cell wall is the structure most clearly visible with a light microscope.

questions.stem: Which one of the following sentences is false?

options.A: The cells of a whale are much larger than that of an ant
options.B: The cells in our body continues to grow and divide to replace the old and damaged cells
options.C: The nucleus controls most of the cellular activities within the cell.
options.D: The cell wall gives plant cells a regular shape

questions.explanation: Cell size is roughly constant across species - whale cells are NOT much larger than ant cells, so statement A is false.

questions.stem: The father of modern taxonomy is _______
questions.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus is the father of modern taxonomy and binomial nomenclature.

questions.stem: _______ is a dynamic and flexible science in which the diversity of organisms and their relationships are studied.
questions.explanation: Systematics is the dynamic science of organism diversity and evolutionary relationships.

questions.stem: The reason for organisms classification includes
questions.explanation: Classification records the world's biodiversity (and has economic value); it never aims to discourage conservation.

questions.stem: Example of natural classification schemes is ____________
questions.explanation: Phenetic (natural) classification groups organisms by overall observable similarity.

questions.stem: _________ is a classification which is based on evolutionary history or pattern of descent.
questions.explanation: Phylogenetic classification is based on evolutionary history and pattern of descent.

questions.stem: The smallest taxonomic rank in the groups below is _______
questions.explanation: Of phylum, order, family and class, family is the smallest (most exclusive) rank.

questions.stem: Oryza sativa belongs to division _______________
questions.explanation: Rice, Oryza sativa, is a flowering plant: division Magnoliophyta.

questions.stem: ________________ have floral parts arranged in multiples of four or five.
questions.explanation: Dicots have floral parts in multiples of four or five; monocots in multiples of three.

questions.stem: Some animals have subspecies, usually caused by geographical locotions and are called
questions.explanation: Names with a subspecies (three words) are trinomials.

questions.stem: Diagram illustrating hierarchy of clades is known as
questions.explanation: A cladogram is the diagram illustrating the hierarchy of clades.

questions.stem: Analysis of amino acids in protein and nucleotides in nucleic acids is termed _____
questions.explanation: Comparative biochemistry analyses amino acids in proteins and nucleotides in nucleic acids.

questions.stem: _____ is an example of animal with radial symmetry
questions.explanation: Sea anemones are radially symmetrical.

questions.stem: Animals with dual embryonic tissue layers are called
questions.explanation: Animals with two embryonic tissue layers (ectoderm and endoderm) are diploblastic.

questions.stem: Classification which examines shapes, sizes and development of organisms is termed
questions.explanation: Comparative morphology examines shapes, sizes and development.

questions.stem: Vertebrates have _______ form of symmetry
questions.explanation: Vertebrates are bilaterally symmetrical.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the kingdom of eukaryotic, multicellular and photo-autotrophic organisms?
questions.explanation: Plantae is the kingdom of eukaryotic, multicellular, photosynthetic organisms.

questions.stem: Plants with soft and delicate stems, usually less than a metre tall are
questions.explanation: Herbs have soft, delicate stems under a metre tall.

questions.stem: Rice, groundnut and potato are
questions.explanation: Rice, groundnut and potato complete their life cycle within one growing season - annuals.

questions.stem: Gymnosperms and Angiosperms belong to
questions.explanation: Seed plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms) belong to the division Spermatophyta.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a monocotyledonous plant?
questions.explanation: Rice is a monocot; groundnut, potato and mango are dicots.

questions.stem: Bryophyta have been placed among cryptogams because

options.C: they do not bear true roots and stems

questions.explanation: Cryptogams reproduce by hidden means (spores) - no flowers or seeds, which is why bryophytes are placed there.

questions.stem: Mosses occur in moist habitat primarily because

options.B: their rate of transpiration is usually very high

questions.explanation: Mosses need a film of water for the flagellated male gametes to swim to the egg.

questions.stem: In the life cycle of plants showing two morphologically distinct phases, the spore represents

options.A: the first cell of the sporophytic phase
options.B: the first cell of the gametophytic phase
options.C: the last cell of the sporophytic phase
options.D: the last cell of the gametophytic phase

questions.explanation: The spore is the first cell of the gametophytic phase - it germinates into the gametophyte.

questions.stem: Gametophytic phase is dominant in the life cycle of
questions.explanation: In bryophytes the gametophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic generation.

questions.stem: Pteridophytes are also called
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes are vascular cryptogams: seedless plants with xylem and phloem.

questions.stem: Which of the following display circinate vernation?
questions.explanation: Both pteridophytes (ferns) and lower gymnosperms (cycads) show circinate vernation - young leaves coiled like a crozier.

questions.stem: Red colour of Rhodophyta is due to
questions.explanation: The red colour of red algae (Rhodophyta) comes from the pigment phycoerythrin.

questions.stem: When seeds of a plant are borne nakedly on megasporophylls and are not enclosed in a fruit wall, the plant belongs to
questions.explanation: Naked seeds borne on megasporophylls without a fruit wall = gymnosperms.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a biennial plant?
questions.explanation: Carrot is a biennial - vegetative growth in year one, flowering and seed in year two.

questions.stem: Secondary growth takes place in most dicotyledonous plants because they possess
questions.explanation: Secondary (width) growth comes from the cambium, present in most dicots.

questions.stem: Garden egg belongs to which of the following angiospermic family?
questions.explanation: Garden egg (eggplant) belongs to the family Solanaceae (nightshades).

questions.stem: A seed is a fertilised
questions.explanation: A seed is a fertilised ovule.

questions.stem: Parallel veination is always present in the leaves of
questions.explanation: Parallel leaf venation characterises monocots.

questions.stem: Cocoa belongs to the family
questions.explanation: Cocoa belongs to Sterculiaceae (sometimes merged into Malvaceae sensu lato).

questions.stem: One of the following belongs to Musaceae
questions.explanation: Plantains and bananas belong to the family Musaceae.

questions.stem: Which is not a component of any taxonomy of living things?

options.B: The organization of similar organisms into groups
options.C: labeling organisms and groups with names
options.D: All of the above are components of any such taxonomy

questions.explanation: Identification, organisation and naming are all components of taxonomy - so 'all of the above are components' is the answer to the 'not' question.

questions.stem: The groups of animals which exist in two body forms of polyp and medusa are called
questions.explanation: Coelenterates (cnidarians) alternate between the polyp and medusa body forms.

questions.stem: The following are classes of the phylum Cnidaria except
questions.explanation: Hydrozoa, Cubozoa, Scyphozoa and Anthozoa are the cnidarian classes; 'Chyozoa' does not exist.

questions.stem: __________ are group of animals which are triploblastic
questions.explanation: Flatworms (Platyhelminthes) are triploblastic - three germ layers.

questions.stem: The following group of animals show cephalization except
questions.explanation: Echinoderms (Asteroidea) show no cephalization; their adults are secondarily radial.

questions.stem: An example of animals of the class Cestoda is
questions.explanation: Tapeworms are cestodes.

questions.stem: An example of a tree-living form of Nematodes is
questions.explanation: Anguillula is a free-living (in some texts tree-living) nematode; the others are parasites or polychaetes.

questions.stem: Octopus belongs to which class of Molluscs?
questions.explanation: Octopus is a cephalopod mollusc.

questions.stem: The mode of feeding of Arachnids is
questions.explanation: Arachnids are carnivorous predators.

questions.stem: An example of the class Diplopoda is
questions.explanation: Millipedes belong to the class Diplopoda.

questions.stem: Centipedes belongs to which class?
questions.explanation: Centipedes belong to the class Chilopoda.

questions.stem: Echinodermata has an endoskeleton which consist of
questions.explanation: The echinoderm endoskeleton is made of calcium carbonate ossicles.

questions.stem: Urochordates are also called
questions.explanation: Urochordates are the tunicates (sea squirts).

questions.stem: The group of fishes without scales belongs to the Superclass
questions.explanation: Agnatha (hagfish, lampreys) lack scales and paired fins.

questions.stem: The group of fishes with skeleton of bones are called
questions.explanation: Osteichthyes are the bony fishes.

questions.stem: __________ is an example of animals that exhibits thermoregulation
questions.explanation: Birds are endotherms - they thermoregulate internally.

questions.stem: The group of animals with mammary glands are
questions.explanation: Mammary glands define the mammals.

questions.stem: Annelids has an ___________ skeleton
questions.explanation: Annelids rely on a hydrostatic skeleton (coelomic fluid under pressure).

questions.stem: Circinate vernation of young leaves occurs in A. Fumaria B. Bryopteris C Pinus D. Selaginella
questions.explanation: Circinate vernation occurs in ferns - Dryopteris.

questions.stem: The father of modern taxonomy is A. Carolus Lintel B. Carolus Livermore C Christian Linnaeus D. Carolus Linnaeus
questions.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus founded modern taxonomy.

questions.stem: Which of the taxonomic categories contains organisms with the largest number of features in common? A Kingdom B Family C Genus D Species
questions.explanation: Species share the largest number of common features.

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences is not a problem with the use of common names in scientific publications? A A particular organism may be known by several different common names B The same name may be given to two quite different organisms C It enables scientists to communicate accurately with each other D None of the above

options.A: A particular organism may be known by several different common names
options.B: The same name may be given to two quite different organisms
options.C: It enables scientists to communicate accurately with each other

questions.explanation: Enabling scientific communication is an ADVANTAGE of scientific names, not a problem of common names.

questions.stem: The advantages of nomenclature in biological classification include all the following except A They are used globally B They are necessary whenever precise identification is required CA particular organism may be known by different vernacular names D Enable scientists to know exactly which organism is being referred to.

options.B: They are necessary whenever precise identification is required
options.C: A particular organism may be known by different vernacular names
options.D: Enable scientists to know exactly which organism is being referred to.

questions.explanation: 'A particular organism may be known by different common names' is a PROBLEM of common names, not an advantage of nomenclature.

questions.stem: In classification, it follows that as one progresses down the hierarchy, the number of organisms in each taxon ________ and the similarities ________ A increases; decreases B increases: increases C decreases: decreases D decreases; increases
questions.explanation: Descending the hierarchy, the number of organisms decreases while features shared in common increase.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is FALSE? A Phenetic classification does not distinguish between homologous and analogous characters B Phylogenetic classification illustrates the hierarchy of ancestors and the degree of evolutionary changes C Family is a group of related organisms ranking above an order and below a genus comprising several species D Systematics is the process of organizing taxonomic information of organisms in logical framework

options.A: Phenetic classification does not distinguish between homologous and analogous characters
options.B: Phylogenetic classification illustrates the hierarchy of ancestors and the degree of evolutionary changes
options.C: Family is a group of related organisms ranking above an order and below a genus comprising several species
options.D: Systematics is the process of organizing taxonomic information of organisms in logical framework

questions.explanation: Family ranks BELOW order and ABOVE genus - statement C reverses it, so C is false.

questions.stem: A system of classification based on all important morphological characters is termed A Artificial system B Natural system C Genetic system D Phenetic system
questions.explanation: A natural system of classification uses all important morphological characters.

questions.stem: The group of similar organisms which breed freely among themselves to produce fertile offspring constitute a ________ A Family B Order C Species D Genus
questions.explanation: Species: similar organisms that interbreed freely to produce fertile offspring.

questions.stem: The five kingdom classifications of organisms was proposed by .... A John Ray B Carl Woese Robert Whittaker D Carolus Linnaeus
questions.explanation: Robert Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification (1969).

questions.stem: The correct binomial nomenclatures of causative agents of malaria and syphilis respectively are:- A Treponema Pallidum and Plasmodium Falciparum B Treponema pallidum and Plasmodium falciparum C Plasmodium Falciparum and Treponema Pallidum Plasmodium falciparum and Treponema pallidum
questions.explanation: Malaria = Plasmodium falciparum; syphilis = Treponema pallidum (species epithets lower-case).

questions.stem: What is the correct descending sequence of hierarchy: (1) Class (2) Kingdom (3) Phylum (4) Order (5) Genus (6) Family (7) Species A 6,2,4,1,5,7,3 B.7,1,3,4,5,6,1 C.2,3,1,4,6,5,7 D.1,2,3,4,5,6,7
questions.explanation: Kingdom(2), Phylum(3), Class(1), Order(4), Family(6), Genus(5), Species(7) gives 2,3,1,4,6,5,7.

questions.stem: The acronym ICZN stands for ...... A International Congress of Zoological Nomenclature B Indian Code of Zoological Nomenclature International code of Zoological Nomenclature D Indian Congress of Zoological Nomenclature
questions.explanation: ICZN = International Code of Zoological Nomenclature.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about phenetic classification: It is based on the A observable characteristics of existing organisms B ancestral lineage of existing organisms C dendogram of DNA characteristics of existing organisms D sexual characteristics of existing organisms

options.C: dendogram of DNA characteristics of existing organisms

questions.explanation: Phenetic classification uses observable characteristics of existing organisms.

options.A: A pamicular organism may be known by several different common names

questions.stem: The group of similar organisms which breed freely aming themselves to produce fertile offspring constitute a ....... A. Family B. Order C. Species D. Genus

questions.stem: What is the correct descending sequence of hiermchy: (1) Class (2) Kingdom (3) Phylum (4) Order (5) Genus (6) Family (7) Species A. 6, 2, 4, 1, 5, 7, 3 B. 7, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 1 C. 2, 3, 1, 4, 6, 5, 7 D. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7

questions.stem: In which kingdom would you classify cyanobacteria, nitrogen fixing and methanogenic bacteria A. Plantae B. Fungi C. Monera D. Protista

questions.stem: Why is photosynthesis important for Plants? A. It collects sunlight which is to make food for plants B. It gets rid of plant waste products C. It changes plant sugar into stronger chemicals. D. It helps attract insects to plant flowers.

options.A: It collects sunlight which is to make food for plants
options.B: It gets rid of plant waste products
options.C: It changes plant sugar into stronger chemicals.
options.D: It helps attract insects to plant flowers.

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis converts sunlight into food (chemical energy) for the plant.

questions.stem: Which of these plants does not have special tissues to deliver food and water to its cells? A. Liverworth B. Maple C. Tomatoe D. Dogwood
questions.explanation: Liverworts are non-vascular - no specialised transport tissue.

questions.stem: Seeds can be dormant for many years until A. Sunlight causes photosynthesis B. Food web are complete C. Conditions are right for growth D. Conduction of food occurs

questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain the green pigment chlorophyll.

questions.stem: One way that mosses and ferns are similar is they are both A. both dormant during the winter B. produce spores C grow in areas with little rainfall D. are flowering plants

options.C: grow in areas with little rainfall

questions.explanation: Mosses and ferns both reproduce by spores.

questions.stem: What do ferns have that apple trees do not have? A. Spores B. Flowers C. Roots D. Stems
questions.explanation: Ferns reproduce by spores; apple trees by seeds.

questions.stem: Pollens is produced in the A. Petal B. Stamen C. Ovary D. Pistil
questions.explanation: Pollen is produced in the stamen (anther).

questions.explanation: Trees, wildflowers and grasses all have vascular tissue - vascular plants.

questions.explanation: Hydra is radially symmetrical.

questions.explanation: Binding away from the active site = non-competitive inhibition.

questions.stem: The goal of homeostasis is the maintenance of equilibrium around a specific value of some aspect of the body or its cells called
questions.explanation: The target value a regulated variable centres on is the set point.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a mechanism to warm the body up in cold weather?
questions.explanation: Vasodilation increases blood flow to the skin and COOLS the body.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: If the glucose concentration falls, the alpha cells release glucagon.
options.B: If the glucose concentration rises, alpha cells release insulin
options.C: If the glucose concentration falls, the beta cells release glucagon
options.D: If the glucose concentration rises, the beta cells release insulin.

questions.explanation: Rising glucose triggers the beta cells to release insulin.

questions.stem: The process of removal of excess water and salts from the body is called
questions.explanation: Osmoregulation manages water and salt balance.

questions.stem: Which hormone increases the permeability of distal convoluted tubule (DCT) and collecting duct (CD) in osmoregulation?
questions.explanation: ADH increases DCT/collecting duct permeability.

questions.stem: Which of the following organs secretes hormones?
questions.explanation: Pancreas, ovaries and the gut all secrete hormones.

questions.stem: The pancreas secretes
questions.explanation: The pancreas secretes insulin and glucagon (from islet cells).

questions.stem: Which of the following glands secretes melatonin?
questions.explanation: The pineal gland secretes melatonin.

questions.stem: Which of these glands secretes oestrogen?
questions.explanation: Oestrogen comes from the ovary.

questions.stem: Which of the following endocrine glands secretes oxytocin?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin is released by the posterior pituitary.

questions.stem: Which of these glands functions both as endocrine and exocrine glands?
questions.explanation: The pancreas is both endocrine (islets) and exocrine (acinar).

questions.stem: Which of the following is/are digestive gland(s)?
questions.explanation: Liver and pancreas are the digestive glands.

questions.stem: Which among the following acts as a valve, allowing only little quantity of food at a time from the stomach into the duodenum?
questions.explanation: The pyloric sphincter meters chyme from stomach to duodenum.

questions.stem: Bile is released by the gall bladder into
questions.explanation: Bile enters the duodenum.

questions.stem: Which of these secretes saliva?
questions.explanation: Saliva comes from the salivary glands.

questions.stem: Villi are present in
questions.explanation: Villi line the ileum (small intestine).

questions.stem: Which of the following does not produce digestive enzyme?
questions.explanation: Bile contains no enzyme - it emulsifies fat.

questions.stem: Where does the digestion of proteins begin?
questions.explanation: Protein digestion begins in the stomach (pepsin).

questions.stem: The layer of the transverse section of generalised gut that suspends and supports the alimentary canal in the abdominal cavity is the
questions.explanation: The serosa suspends and supports the gut.

questions.stem: Offsprings of asexual reproduction show
questions.explanation: Asexual offspring are genetically identical - only minor (mutational) variation.

questions.stem: On which side of your abdomen does the stomach lie?
questions.explanation: The stomach lies on the left side of the abdomen.

questions.stem: Which of the following is necessary for the release of energy present in food?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is needed to release food energy (aerobic respiration).

questions.stem: Diffusion of oxygen from blood to tissues and diffusion of carbon dioxide from tissues to blood is known as
questions.explanation: Gas exchange between blood and tissues is tissue (internal) respiration.

questions.stem: The fusion of the male reproductive nucleus and the female reproductive nucleus is termed
questions.explanation: Fusion of male and female nuclei = fertilization.

questions.stem: What does mitosis aim at?

options.A: Chromosomes move away from one another to opposite poles of the spindle
options.B: Assorts the replicated genetic materials to daughter cells equally
options.C: Assorts the replicated genetic materials to daughter cells randomly

questions.explanation: Mitosis assorts replicated genetic material EQUALLY into daughter cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following organelles is responsible for producing vesicles that contains cell plate materials?
questions.explanation: The Golgi packages cell-plate material into vesicles.

questions.stem: An inheritance pattern in which the alleles are neither dominant nor recessive is referred to as
questions.explanation: Codominance: neither allele dominant (both expressed).

questions.stem: The main characteristics of growth are: (I) Cellular growth (II) Cell division (III) Cell expansion (IV) Cellular differentiation. A. I and II only B. I, II and IV only C. All of the above D. None of the above.
questions.explanation: Cellular growth, division, expansion and differentiation all characterize growth.

questions.stem: Growth characterised by initial slow growth, followed by a rapid increase in growth, followed by a phase where growth slows down and finally no growth is referred to as
questions.explanation: Slow-rapid-slow (S-curve) = geometric growth.

questions.stem: Which of these process(es) is/are involved in cell division?
questions.explanation: Interphase, mitosis and cytokinesis are all part of the cell division cycle.

questions.stem: Genome in which chromosomes occur in pairs are said to be diploid, and the members of a pair are called
questions.explanation: Paired chromosomes are homologues.

questions.stem: Gregor Mendel is often called
questions.explanation: Mendel is the father of genetics.

questions.stem: What are genes?

options.A: Something that you wear on your legs
options.B: Segments of DNA that carry instructions for the traits of the offspring

questions.explanation: Genes are DNA segments carrying instructions.

questions.stem: The passing of traits from parents to offspring is called
questions.explanation: Trait passage parent-to-offspring = heredity.

questions.stem: An organism with two different alleles for a trait is said to be
questions.explanation: Two different alleles = hybrid (heterozygote).

questions.stem: What would be the results of a genetic cross between two parents that have a BB and a Bb?
questions.explanation: BB x Bb gives BB, BB, Bb, Bb.

questions.stem: If the results of a genetic cross were RR, RR, Rr, rr What would be the probability of getting a purebred smooth? Note that R is dominant (smooth) and r is recessive (wrinkled)
questions.explanation: Purebred (RR + rr) = 2 of 4 = 50%.

questions.stem: Which of the following genotypes is considered to be heterozygous?
questions.explanation: Tt is heterozygous.

questions.stem: Flaty is an example of
questions.explanation: The platypus is a monotreme.

questions.stem: Incurrent pores in sponges is called
questions.explanation: Incurrent sponge pores are ostia.

questions.stem: Myxobolus pfeifferi belongs to
questions.explanation: Myxobolus, a myxosporidan, belongs to Cnidospora.

questions.stem: Homo sapiens is an example of
questions.explanation: Humans are placental mammals - Eutheria.

questions.stem: Growth in animals is _______ while growth in plants is _______

options.A: Diffused and continuous; apical and regenerative.
options.B: Diffused and ceases at a stage; apical and continuous.
options.C: Regenerative and intercalary; lateral and discontinuous.
options.D: Localized and continuous; apical and ceases at a stage.

questions.explanation: Animal growth is diffused and ceases at maturity; plant growth is apical (localized) and continuous.

questions.stem: Study this reaction: Energy + Carbondioxide + water ->Carbohydrate + Oxygen. This chemical transformation is called _______
questions.explanation: CO2 + water + energy -> carbohydrate + O2 is photosynthesis.

questions.stem: Which organelle is responsible for this chemical transformation: Carbohydrate + Oxygen ->Energy+ Carbondioxide + water?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrate + O2 -> energy + CO2 happens in mitochondria.

questions.stem: What is the function of the centrosome?

options.D: To control the movement of cilia

questions.explanation: The centrosome organises spindle microtubules - cell division.

questions.stem: Plants absorb mineral nutrients in the form of ____________ from the soil
questions.explanation: Mineral nutrients are absorbed as a weak (dilute) solution of ions.

questions.stem: Animal cells do not synthesize their own food, therefore they are _____________
questions.explanation: Animal cells are heterotrophic.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures do plants and animals have in common?

options.A: Mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, chloroplast and vacuoles.
options.B: Mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, golgi bodies and nucleus
options.C: Mitochondria, chloroplasts, endoplasmic reticulum and cell wall.
options.D: Golgi bodies, nucleus, centrosomes and vacuoles

questions.explanation: Mitochondria, ER, Golgi and nucleus occur in both kingdoms.

questions.stem: Food is stored mainly as ___________ in plants while in animals, excess food is stored as ___________.
questions.explanation: Plants store starch; animals store glycogen.

questions.stem: _________ is a green pigment found within grana that makes chloroplasts and leaves green
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment in the grana.

questions.stem: Most of the plants remain anchored to the soil and are ___________, while animals can move physically from one place to another and so are ___________
questions.explanation: Plants are sessile; animals motile.

questions.stem: Which comparison between plant and animal cells is NOT correct?

options.A: Plants: cell wall; animals: no cell wall
options.B: Plants: large, single vacuole; animals: many, small vacuoles
options.D: Plants: absorb mineral salts; animals: take solid food

questions.explanation: It is ANIMALS that have centrosomes - C reverses it.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is FALSE?

options.A: Cell walls are found in plants but not in animals.
options.B: Cell walls are found inside the plasma membrane of a cell.
options.C: The main constituent of a primary cell wall is cellulose molecules.
options.D: Secondary cell walls contain lignin, a substance that makes them stronger than primary cell walls.

questions.explanation: The cell wall lies OUTSIDE the plasma membrane, not inside.

questions.stem: Scientists decide whether an organism is a plant or animal based on A.whether it is multicellular or unicellular B. whether it is mobile or not C. how it reproduces D.how it obtains its food or energy

options.A: whether it is multicellular or unicellular
options.B: whether it is mobile or not
options.D: how it obtains its food or energy

questions.explanation: Nutrition (how it obtains food/energy) separates plant from animal.

questions.stem: Which one of the following sentences is false? A. The cells of a whale are much larger than that of an ant B. The cells in our body continues to grow and divide to replace the old and damaged cells C. The nucleus controls most of the cellular activities within the cell. D. The cell wall gives plant cells a regular shape

options.A: The cells of a whale are much larger than that of an ant
options.B: The cells in our body continues to grow and divide to replace the old and damaged cells
options.C: The nucleus controls most of the cellular activities within the cell.
options.D: The cell wall gives plant cells a regular shape

questions.explanation: Whale cells are not much larger than ant cells - A is false.

questions.stem: The father of modern taxonomy is ____________ A.Robert Hooke B. Francesco Redi C. Carlos Linnaeus D. Edward Jenner
questions.explanation: Carolus (Carlos) Linnaeus, father of taxonomy.

questions.stem: __________________ is a dynamic and flexible science in which the diversity of organisms and their relationships are studied. A.Taxonomy B. Nomenclature C. Systematics D. all of the above.
questions.explanation: Systematics studies diversity and relationships.

questions.stem: The reason for organisms classification includes A.economic reason B. recording the world's biodiversity C. discourage conservation of organisms D. none of the above.
questions.explanation: Classification records biodiversity.

questions.stem: Example of natural classification schemes is _____________ A.Phenetic B. Family C. Order D. Taxon.
questions.explanation: Phenetic classification is the natural scheme.

questions.stem: _____________ is a classification which is based on evolutionary history or pattern of descent. A.Phylogenetics B. Phenetic C. Genetics D. All of the above.
questions.explanation: Phylogenetics follows evolutionary descent.

questions.stem: The smallest taxonomic rank in the groups below is ________ A.Phylum B. Order C. Family D. Class
questions.explanation: Family is the smallest rank listed.

questions.stem: Oryza sativa belongs to division ___________ A.Magnoliophyta B. Pooles C. Poaceae D. None of the above.
questions.explanation: Oryza sativa: Magnoliophyta.

questions.stem: ____________ have floral parts arranged in multiples of four or five. A.Monocots B. Cycadophyta C. Dicots D. All of the above.
questions.explanation: Dicots: floral parts in 4s and 5s.

questions.stem: Some animals have subspecies, usually caused by geographical locations and are called A.Binomials B. Trinomials C. Eukarya D. Monera
questions.explanation: Trinomials name subspecies.

questions.stem: Diagram illustrating hierarchy of clades is known as A.phylogenetic tree B. cladogram C. ancestral tree D. all of the above
questions.explanation: Cladogram: the clade hierarchy diagram.

questions.stem: Analysis of amino acids in protein and nucleotides in nucleic acids is termed ______ A.competitive cytology B. comparative biochemistry C. cladogram D. phylogenetic information.
questions.explanation: Comparative biochemistry.

questions.stem: _______ is an example of animal with radial symmetry A.Sponge B. Sea anemone C. Lizard D. Bats
questions.explanation: Sea anemone: radial symmetry.

questions.stem: Animals with dual embryonic tissue layers are called A.Diploblastic B. Endoderm C. Triploblastic D. All of the above.
questions.explanation: Diploblastic.

questions.stem: Classification which examines shapes, sizes and development of organisms is termed A.competitive cytology. B. comparative morphology C. comparative biochemistry D. all of the above.
questions.explanation: Comparative morphology.

questions.stem: Vertebrates have ________ form of symmetry. A.radial B. bilateral C. asymmetry D. none of the above.
questions.explanation: Bilateral symmetry in vertebrates.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the kingdom of eukaryotic, multicellular and photo-autotrophic organisms? A.Fungi B. Animalia C. Protoctista D. Plantae
questions.explanation: Plantae.

questions.stem: Plants with soft and delicate stems, usually less than a metre tall are A. herbs B. shrubs C. trees D. liana
questions.explanation: Herbs.

questions.stem: Bryophytes have been placed among cryptogams because

options.C: they do not bear true roots and stems

questions.explanation: Bryophytes are cryptogams because they produce no flowers - reproduction is hidden (spores).
